title: Why empires let go
question: Why did colonial powers give up their colonies?
hook: Empires that once seemed permanent ended in two centuries, and scholars still disagree about why.
idea: Several pressures worked together: new ideas, falling profits, and shrinking support at home for holding colonies.

beats.prompt: Two empires each fight rebels in a faraway colony, one in the 19th century and one in the 20th. Which is more likely to have strong backing from its own public?

choices.label: The 19th-century empire, with strong political will behind it
The 20th-century empire, whose public sees colonies as a prize
choices.feedback: It tempts because empires look strong, but by then publics were apathetic and holding colonies was often seen as a burden.

choices.label: Both equally, since empires always have loyal publics
choices.feedback: It tempts as a simple rule, but the explanation says conditions changed between the centuries.

beats.explain: In the 19th century colonial powers had strong political will and regional support; in the 20th century they faced apathetic publics and hostile superpowers.

beats.prompt: Put these moments of decolonization in order
items: Thirteen North American colonies declare independence from Britain
Latin American independence wars begin with a revolt in La Paz
Palau becomes independent and Hong Kong and Macau are handed over
beats.explain: The United States came in 1776, Haiti in 1804, the Latin American wars in 1809, and the last wave after the Cold War.

beats.prompt: Match each explanation of decolonization to its claim
pairs: More education led to calls for popular sovereignty
Wage labor and a bigger bourgeois class drove it
Lower profitability and the costs of empire
beats.explain: Each analysis points to a different cause for the spread of anti-colonial movements.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: Many colonies gained independence in the two centuries after 1783.
Rising education in the colonies fed calls for popular sovereignty.
So one cause explains every case, and no other explanation is needed.
Other analyses point to costs and profitability instead.
beats.explain: Several analyses give different reasons for the spread of anti-colonial movements, so no single cause covers every case.
